sentences.text: Steneosaurus was an extinct teleosaurid crocodyliform, a group of marine reptiles related to modern crocodilians.
The genus is currently considered a nomen dubium because its defining specimen lacks clear diagnostic features.
The original material was found in three fragments by Abbot Charles Bacheley near Villers-sur-Mer, France.
Georges Cuvier was the first to illustrate the front parts of this type specimen in 1808.
The specific name Steneosaurus rostromajor was officially established in 2020.
Historically, the name served as a wastebasket taxon for many unrelated fossils.
A 2005 analysis revealed that the group is not monophyletic, leading researchers to divide traditional species into longirostrine and mesorostrine skull groups.
Recent studies suggest that Steneosaurus obtusidens is actually the sister species of Machimosaurus and has been renamed Lemmysuchus.
It is debated whether the remaining species are related, as many are considered paraphyletic or polyphyletic, suggesting they require new generic names.
The type species lived in Western Europe during the Callovian stage, while S. edwardsi inhabited England and France during the Callovian and Oxfordian.
However, the Paleobiology Database records a broader time range for the genus from the Toarcian to the Berriasian, spanning 184.2 to 141 million years ago.
